title: Ethiopian Amete Alem Calendar
intro: A separate Ethiopian year-counting tradition. Amete Alem dates use the thirteen-month Ethiopian year structure but a different count of years from Amete Mihret.
summary: Twelve 30-day months and a short thirteenth month. Amete Alem year numbers are 5,500 higher than Amete Mihret year numbers.
origin: Amete Alem means 'Year of the World'. It is a separate Ethiopian era convention, not an alias for the Amete Mihret count.
structure: Twelve months have thirty days each. The thirteenth, Pagume, has five days in an ordinary year or six in a leap year.
pattern_note: A calendar date can have the same month and day in the Amete Mihret and Amete Alem systems while carrying very different year numbers.
history: Ethiopian calendar traditions use different eras for numbering years. The Amete Alem count is especially important when interpreting historical and religious year references.
example: If a date is year 2018 in Amete Mihret, the same date is year 7518 in Amete Alem under this 5,500-year convention.
limits: This provider implements the Amete Alem arithmetic and its own era. It does not replace the separate Amete Mihret calendar, nor does mathematical continuation certify every historical use.
